main_body: Half-timbered house: a large hipped tile roof over a cream plaster wall with timber framing, a gabled front porch and a chimney
top_band: Brown tile roof slope, rows ~10-42 at a left-wing column (lighter tan tile highlights on the left slope), a big foreshortened top surface
evidence: In a column through the left wing, the roof tile slope runs from about row 10 to 42, then a dark eave line at rows 42-44 casts shade, then the plaster and timber wall runs from row 44 to 74. The front gable and hip ridges show the roof slopes as real surfaces. The windows and doors have dark inset frames. The roof and wall are both clearly drawn, so this is a correct 3/4 building.

style.evidence: The roof tiles carry per-tile texture and a few steps (highlight tan, light, mid, dark, deep maroon), which is decent. The plaster walls are large flat cream areas of 5x5 pixels or more with no speckle, grain or shading, whereas the references have speckled plaster and stone shaded one by one. The timber is a flat dark maroon with little ramp. The outer silhouette outline is close to near-black, while the interior lines are tinted brown. Tiles on the wall and porch hold only about 2-4 colours, so the piece reads thinner and flatter than the references.
